The source omits the outcome and action mapping (source lines 13 and 19). In Checkout, voucher creation and form submission lead to pending status (`payment_intent.requires_action`, `checkout.session.completed`), with `checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded` for successful store payment and `checkout.session.async_payment_failed` for expiry or other failure (old raw lines 186–212). The separate November overview lines 9–17 and 192–214 reinforce asynchronous confirmation after cash payment. Funds availability after four business days is a separate statement in that overview, not voucher creation, payment success, or bank deposit timing.

historical_claims_to_preserve: May 7, 2026 Checkout only documents `expires_after_days` (1–60 calendar days, default three; cutoff 23:59:59 JST). Direct API documents that day-count setting or mutually exclusive Unix-second `expires_at` with lead-time checks at setting and confirmation and an upper bound of less than 60 days after it is set. If neither is set, Direct API states three days after PaymentIntent creation at 23:59 JST (old raw lines 105–115 and 434–450). Checkout testing references to an `expires_at` override in output are not Checkout request-schema evidence (old raw lines 214–245).

Keep May Checkout optional phone-as-confirmation-number and random fallback (old raw lines 180–184), distinct from Direct API optional 10–11 digit `confirmation_number`, random fallback when absent, all-zero blocking at creation/update/confirmation, and possible rejection for a number too common among ongoing transactions at confirmation (old raw lines 555–569). The optional up-to-22-character Shift JIS `product_description` is documented for Direct API (old raw lines 434–442). Preserve the May Dahlia Stripe.js example as dated (old raw lines 493–516).

Keep the expiry buffer and state-changing actions dated. New kiosk initiation stops at `expires_at`; a valid slip issued before the deadline may still be payable at the register. After an unpaid buffer, the PaymentIntent returns to `requires_payment_method`. Updating the Intent or confirming with another payment method implicitly cancels a pending Konbini payment; cancellation fails if the shopper is currently paying, invalidates old instructions when successful, and successful reconfirmation in `requires_action` creates new instructions and a new URL. Availability issues also affect cancellations (old raw lines 247–261 and 815–840).

Keep bank-transfer refund states dated to the full May guide (old raw lines 263–286 and 842–865): `requires_action` waiting for bank details, `pending` after customer submission, `succeeded` when expected to arrive, and `requires_action` again if the bank returns funds. The 45-day failure is for a refund still in `requires_action` 45 days after creation; `refund.failed` requires returning the funds outside Stripe. Optional instruction/reminder emails and special confirmation-number/email timing overrides have Dashboard or test-only qualifications (old raw lines 744–752 and 784–813).
conflicts: Reciprocal product-versus-document boundary: source line 17 states “no Elements path,” the new acceptance index lines 9–14 lists only Checkout and Direct API, and the separately dated product overview explicitly lists Payment Element (November overview lines 157–165; May overview lines 70–83 lists Elements). Keep the acceptance guide variants separate from product availability in both the acceptance summary and voucher concept route. A missing index link is not evidence of lack of support, removal, or a Checkout Sessions-versus-PaymentIntents implementation for Payment Element.

Source line 19 gives event shorthand and calls all three async. Separate Direct API PaymentIntent events and give readers a scoped fulfillment distinction (old raw lines 186–212 and 754–768).

Source line 33's unqualified 45-day deadline refers specifically to a refund still in `requires_action` after creation (old raw lines 434–450 and 263–286).

Preserve the qualified exception reciprocally where payment timing is summarized; no fixed completion or cancellation guarantee follows.

The May `payment_method_types` writes on Checkout Session Create and PaymentIntent Create (old raw lines 43-49, 69-74, 95-101 and 131-148) are historical. Separate Stripe changelogs specify HTTP 400 if these Create requests pass `payment_method_types` to their linked `2026-09-30.endive` REST endpoints. Checkout still shows the computed compatible list in the response. PaymentIntent rejects the writable parameter with `payment_method_types_no_longer_supported` and retains a read-only computed property. The Intent changelog's Impact paragraph separately says `2026-08-26.preview`, while its endpoint and REST table links use `2026-09-30.endive`. Preserve both labels rather than assigning a rollout start. The documented alternatives are Dashboard-managed dynamic methods, optional request exclusions using `excluded_payment_method_types`, or `allowed_payment_method_types`, which filters out incompatible methods. Filtering does not guarantee display of `kr_card`. The REST warning belongs at the May samples in source lines 30-41 and the reciprocal Korea route. It does not originate in November's navigation-only capture or the old Stripe.js Dahlia example (raw/stripe-changelog-endive-2026-09-30-remove-payment-method-types-checkout-sessions-2026-11-07.md:9-23,27-32 and raw/stripe-changelog-endive-2026-09-30-removes-the-payment-method-types-parameter-from-payment-intents-and-setup-intents-2026-11-07.md:9-24,28,34-36).

Keep the embedded Checkout page distinct from excluded Elements, and the mobile pointer scoped to the separate iOS app-to-browser Checkout instructions in supported markets.

Replace the source line 24 dispute row with the November decision and fee conditions (new raw lines 93-101). In November’s documented dispute workflow, Stripe uses automated tools and manual review, can accept if it expects the seller is unlikely to win, and submits evidence without requesting more from the seller when it decides to counter. findings: April and November agree that Managed Payments is Stripe’s merchant-of-record product for digital goods via Checkout or Payment Links. Link is the buyer-facing identity from checkout through orders and transaction support, including “Sold through Link” and the LINK.COM* descriptor. The seller retains product support and can issue refunds and update subscriptions in Dashboard/API, subject to the specific payment-method exception. Stripe calculates/collects/files/remits covered indirect tax in more than 80 countries and withholds applicable tax on completion; outside its coverage the seller remains responsible and can use Stripe Tax to calculate tax at no additional charge. Old raw lines 8-34 and 62-87; new raw lines 9-42 and 64-91; mapped source lines 13-40.

Both document guest or Link-account checkout, guest onboarding for order management, configurable terms/privacy links, Link PDFs and receipt-setting independence, trial-start and longer-than-seven-day trial-end notices, standard renewal/card/failure controls, and Stripe-managed fraud rules/blocklists. An escalation goes to the configured support email; lack of merchant response within 48 hours can lead to a refund without approval. Stripe can refund within 60 days in certain cases; customer refunds include tax, with separate seller balance impact in certain jurisdictions. Old raw lines 23-58 and 64-87; new raw lines 23-60 and 66-91; source lines 19-46. The source’s table wording ‘seller escalated within 48h’ at line 22 misidentifies the clock despite its correct detailed rule at lines 35-37.

Both list tables conditioned on customer country, one-time versus recurring mode, local presentment and Adaptive Pricing support; default Adaptive Pricing does the presentment work when the method supports it. Konbini and WeChat Pay are prose examples of local payment methods and absent from both Managed Payments matrices. Neither general checkout text nor a method row guarantees that a method is displayed for a particular session or that payment succeeds. Old raw lines 27-29 and 89-114; new raw lines 27-29 and 103-128; source lines 54-72.

Both allow requested deletion across Managed Payments transactions and the associated Link account, cancel subscriptions sold through Managed Payments, remove customer information from related v2 Account, Customer, PaymentMethod, Invoice, PaymentIntent, Subscription and Charge objects including related merchant-side objects, and notify the seller by email on receipt of the request. That says customer data is deleted from relevant objects, with the notification tied to request receipt. Old raw lines 120-128; new raw lines 144-152; source lines 48-52.

The how-it-works comparison itself sets no new API-version floor. The distinct generic Klarna subscription and Bancontact generated-SEPA routes are scoped separately in wiki/concepts/stripe-klarna.md lines 14-27 and wiki/concepts/stripe-bancontact.md lines 12-20; the Managed Payments matrix controls its own route.

April says Smart Disputes automatically submits evidence in most cases and a merchant can manually submit evidence (old raw line 19). Merchant-added but unsubmitted evidence can be reviewed and submitted by Stripe at no evidence-submission fee to the merchant. New raw lines 19-19 and 93-101; source line 24. This establishes workflow and fee distinctions without specifying fee amounts, prevalence or dispute outcomes.

findings: Both captures describe Stripe-hosted browser Checkout for eligible iOS digital goods or subscriptions in some countries, with Stripe as merchant of record and the Link customer-facing experience. The Merchant of Record role and the app's own user, Stripe Customer and entitlement ledger are distinct. The merchant maps user to Customer server-side to recover purchases, then creates a Checkout Session using a Price in line_items, customer, mode, managed_payments.enabled, origin_context mobile_app and a Universal Link success_url. Compare raw/stripe-managed-payments-mobile-2025.md:4-12,125-154,210-256,268-303,514-520 with raw/stripe-payments-managed-payments-set-up-mobile-2026-11-07.md:5-9,142-173,229-276,288-323,536-542. Stripe/Link roles are corroborated by raw/stripe-payments-managed-payments-how-it-works-2026-11-07.md:9-29.

All products in the purchase must be eligible, including eligible tax codes, with Dashboard activation, development setup and API 2025-03-31.basil or later in both captures (raw/stripe-managed-payments-mobile-2025.md:25-43, raw/stripe-payments-managed-payments-set-up-mobile-2026-11-07.md:36-54). Some-country external-link scope, product eligibility, StoreKit device purchase restrictions and actual merchant eligibility are separate. The Swift sample checks canMakePayments() for parental controls and opens Safari, and the Universal Link is an app return with a fallback page. User authentication and native StoreKit IAP implementation are outside guide scope. See raw/stripe-payments-managed-payments-set-up-mobile-2026-11-07.md:36-50,175-227,335-379, and wiki/sources/source-stripe-managed-payments-mobile.md:13,30-45,51-54. The baseline's 'MoR-compliant' language at line 13 would overstate App Store or regulatory approval.

The baseline summary wiki/sources/source-stripe-managed-payments-mobile.md:38-45 presents checkout.session.completed as sufficient to grant entitlement. Both captures describe server fulfillment after successful payment, map session.customer to the app user and use session.id in a coin transaction example. Redirect can happen after event acknowledgement or after 10 seconds when it is not acknowledged after a successful payment and is an app UI/refresh signal. See raw/stripe-managed-payments-mobile-2025.md:341-352,408-467, raw/stripe-payments-managed-payments-set-up-mobile-2026-11-07.md:360-373,429-489. The related general Managed Payments guide differentiates completion, asynchronous success and asynchronous failure (raw/stripe-payments-managed-payments-set-up-2026-11-07.md:398-408, raw/stripe-managed-payments-setup-2025.md:452-464). Conditional on a delayed method being offered, ordinary Checkout's delayed-method guide explains that Session completion can mean debit authorization and to wait for payment success before fulfillment (raw/stripe-checkout-dashboard-payment-methods-2025.md:66-84). Use verified server events and confirm paid outcome before granting credits, with an idempotent per-Session entitlement operation as supported by the reciprocal non-MoR route (wiki/sources/source-stripe-inapp-digital-goods-checkout.md:25-32). The mobile sample does not prove delayed-method availability, payment or fulfillment execution, or end-to-end idempotency.

The mobile webhook sample is illustrative. It shows signature verification with the raw body using the configured secret, also includes an unsigned fallback, and then references event outside its local declaration instead of the extracted data (raw/stripe-managed-payments-mobile-2025.md:423-460, raw/stripe-payments-managed-payments-set-up-mobile-2026-11-07.md:445-482). This is a retained sample defect/limitation, not a new integration behavior or a production-ready handler. Webhook acknowledgement and entitlement persistence are distinct from the browser return.

Both captures state Managed Payments subscription authorization is limited to charges by Managed Payments and that appropriate consent is needed for transactions outside it (raw/stripe-managed-payments-mobile-2025.md:493-495, raw/stripe-payments-managed-payments-set-up-mobile-2026-11-07.md:515-517). The summary omits this operational boundary (wiki/sources/source-stripe-managed-payments-mobile.md:11-45). Preserve the separate app user/Customer mapping and entitlement ownership, and avoid inferring authorization portability or product-level support delegation from the Link checkout identity.

findings: Current summary lines 13–19 describe full cross-platform coverage, but the implementation content is primarily Swift. For a reader asking how to set up rather than charge, or how to mount the Element in Android or React Native, route to the nine dated April variants and distinguish SetupIntent from PaymentIntent and the server/webhook boundary (old 10–20, 293–330, 604–610, 747–759, 1189–1199, 2380–2405, 3870–4020, 4940–4975, 6544–6650 and 7453–7457). Untargeted navigation into the 9,657-line old raw obscures these essential differences.

Current summary lines 16–19 and 59–76 need platform and mode scope. The dated iOS guide requires a scrollable container such as UIScrollView in UIKit or ScrollView in SwiftUI, and passes presentingViewController and delegate in UIKit. Android classic views use ComposeView and the Element content must be scrollable. The Android cart example invokes configure again, while UIKit/SwiftUI and React Native use update; React Native’s native Android view must remain mounted. The iOS form-sheet example optionally confirms the chosen flow immediately after a customer action, with the result callback after dismissal and no reuse after completion, while setup mode immediately confirms setup without charging (old 110–146, 264–286, 333–406, 579–601, 1794–1815, 3899–4016, 4155–4179, 6612–6616 and 6683–6690).

Current summary lines 68–86 omit that confirmation and the UI result can precede an asynchronous payment’s outcome. Distinguish setup completion, delayed payment processing, success and failure. Keep trusted server price calculation and matched IntentConfiguration, server confirmation or SDK confirmation as appropriate to the documented path, and payment fulfillment decisions on server-side events rather than the app result. Preserve mandate placement and working links if rendered manually (old 320–328, 548–576, 604–610, 747–759 and 905–929).

Current summary line 55 uses `.billing_details` as though it were a verified Swift property. The dated UIKit guide supports access to billing details in prose but does not specify that identifier at old lines 249–260. Retain the concept, omit the unverified spelling.

Current summary line 13 presents full cross-platform coverage but gives no targeted route to two April prerequisites. In the setup and pay-and-save variants, attach the payment method for future payment to the object that represents the customer, either an Accounts v2 customer-configured Account or a Customers v1 Customer. On React Native iOS, Stripe cannot present payment methods that require a return URL when one is missing, even if they are enabled. This dated SDK route uses a custom URL scheme forwarded to Stripe (old 1277–1288, 2489–2500, 6890–6900, 7537–7548, 7900–7910 and 8992–9002).

April Android examples show `false` for the Android builder, which does not resolve the Swift discrepancy (old 548–576, 1763–1792, 2979–3008 and 4136–4154). Record a source warning and route the concept’s mandate reference to it.

The April iOS setup prose names a SetupIntent from the server and then says the Element confirms a PaymentIntent. Use the setup variant identity and same-variant setup-mode/server descriptions, supported by explicit Android and React Native SetupIntent confirmation, and label the contradictory April iOS wording as historical (old 1189–1199, 1336–1347, 1535–1537, 1724–1726, 1817–1889, 4939–4957 and 7833–7835). The historically documented app-controlled default and optional iOS/Android in-sheet confirmation coexist, and the dated embedded iOS SDK callback uses a custom scheme, distinct from separate app-to-web Universal Link flows described at concept lines 83–84 and 107–110 (old 100–106, 579–601, 680–745, 4155–4179, 6890–6950).

The concept says consent collection automatically handles compliance at line 67. In this dated embedded save flow the merchant is responsible for compliance, explicit use-specific consent and written agreement records, with `allow_redisplay` distinguishing whether attached methods may be shown (old 2395–2405, 3198–3206 and 8554–8565). CustomerSession features enable UI controls and cannot establish compliance. Qualify the concept and reciprocally link the source guidance.

findings: The mapped summary wiki/sources/source-stripe-inapp-display-bnpl-messaging.md:17-29 accurately captures April's platform opt-ins and loading APIs. UIKit calls async create and attaches its successful native view; config changes recreate the view. SwiftUI applies configuration with @State-based refresh, offers loaded/loading/noContent/failed phases, and manually created viewData can render immediately. Android uses the separate example artifact com.stripe:payment-method-messaging:23.5.0, application context and configure result Succeeded/NoContent/Failed, with Compose Content updating on configure. The current summary's all-platform scope risks implying Android Apple Pay, and the unqualified iOS table can route maintainers to an inaccurate enum spelling for retained 26.11.0.

Source lines 17–22 make Apple Pay an all-platform fact. The April Embedded guide shows Apple Pay in its iOS and React Native prose and repeats it in the Android paragraph (old raw lines 12-20,63-71,139-147). The related April PaymentSheet guide explicitly names Google Pay for Android (`raw/stripe-inapp-filter-card-brands-2025.md:63-82`), and the April Embedded integration separately documents Android Google Pay configuration (`raw/stripe-inapp-accept-payment-embedded-2025.md:4423-4447`). React Native 0.84.0 explicitly scopes Embedded `applePay` to iOS and `googlePay` to Android (`src/types/EmbeddedPaymentElement.tsx:133-145`, snapshot 2026-10-29-33ef1ee). Keep that platform and UI scope in the source and reciprocal in-app concept. Google Pay setup and a passed brand filter parameter do not alone verify that a particular Google Pay card/network is filtered by Embedded, and a separately configured standalone wallet button is a distinct route (`raw/stripe-inapp-accept-payment-embedded-2025.md:930-936,4423-4444`).

Source lines 26–27 and 73–78 treat the April iOS enum spelling and namespace difference as generic. The retained iOS StripePaymentSheet 26.11.0 snapshot 2026-09-30-7037819 exposes an Embedded `Configuration.cardBrandAcceptance` property but declares `EmbeddedPaymentElement.CardBrandAcceptance` and `BrandCategory` as aliases to `PaymentSheet.CardBrandAcceptance` and its category (`EmbeddedPaymentElementConfiguration.swift:133-138`, `EmbeddedPaymentElement.swift:593-611`, `PaymentSheetConfiguration.swift:846-871`, module version `StripePaymentSheet.podspec:1-9`). Date the April namespace wording, preserve the distinct configuration object, and qualify the reciprocal concept at line 101 and Stripe index route at line 115. Android's April Embedded builder takes the shared PaymentSheet category (old raw lines 89-128). The retained Android 23.25.1 PaymentSheet snapshot confirms the shared type and default/all/allow/disallow API (`PaymentSheet.kt:1185-1196,3540-3602` and `gradle.properties:25-27`), without proving every Embedded wallet path.

The retained iOS 26.11.0 Embedded setting explicitly describes a client-side control and no Link support. It filters Apple Pay's request networks and defaults to `.all` (`EmbeddedPaymentElementConfiguration.swift:133-138`). React Native 0.84.0 also says Embedded brand filtering is client-side and Link is unsupported, retains the brand category and all/allow/disallow union, and forwards the setting through its native Embedded paths (`src/types/EmbeddedPaymentElement.tsx:191-197`, `src/types/PaymentSheet.ts:743-789`, `ios/StripeSdkImpl+Embedded.swift:337-344`, `EmbeddedPaymentElementViewManager.kt:150-165`). These controls do not establish server-side authorization or payment outcome.

React Native 0.84.0's Android bridge returns `all()` if an allow/disallow list is missing or maps to no recognized brands. Its iOS bridge, for a provided array, returns the filtered list even if empty (`PaymentElementConfig.kt:220-253`, `StripeSdkImpl+PaymentSheet.swift:261-299`). Scope those edge cases to the retained bridge code and avoid assuming cross-platform malformed/empty-list handling or a fail-closed policy. Source lines 17–22 currently state filtering too categorically. The April example supplied nonempty known brands.

The old React Native endpoint returns `customerSessionClientSecret`, but both identity branches of its client example instead expect `ephemeralKey` and pass `customerEphemeralKeySecret`; its optional custom flow also uses an ephemeral-key example (old raw 2098–2103, 2144–2149, 2248–2355, 2884–2897). The old captures of the integration distinguish selection, completing the sheet, and later success or failure; the `processing` row separately describes a pending state and an optional digital-goods decision (old raw 549–552, 620–632, 1868–1924, 2411–2413, 2486–2498). The archived text does not make earlier fulfillment a signal of payment success.

The in-app concept lines 58–67 can conflate a broader saved-method matrix with the narrower historical `setup_future_usage` limit and says automatic consent handles global compliance. The old guide explicitly assigns responsibility for the intended future use to the merchant and requires purpose-specific consent (old raw 22–33, 115–130, 634–638). A reciprocal source route should warn about both distinctions. The saved-method concept’s mobile route at line 154 should be date-scoped and preserve the distinction from its web `payment_element` example at lines 46–67.

Source lines 77–82 and the April example at old raw lines 473-508 use `useStripe().handleCardAction`. The retained `@stripe/stripe-react-native` snapshot `2026-10-29-33ef1ee` identifies version 0.84.0 in `package.json:1-9`. `CHANGELOG.md:1138-1146` records removal of `handleCardAction` in 0.7.0 in favor of `handleNextAction`. The 0.84.0 hook exposes the replacement and its implementation accepts the PaymentIntent client secret and optional return URL (`src/hooks/useStripe.tsx:114-122,330-367`, `src/functions.ts:173-201`). Add a version-qualified warning beside the old example and in the reciprocal in-app route (`wiki/concepts/stripe-inapp-payments.md:115`).

The retained `stripe-ios` snapshot `2026-09-30-7037819` identifies 26.11.0 (`StripePayments.podspec:1-8`). `STPPaymentHandler.swift:2770-2779` deprecates the exact Objective-C selector `handleNextActionForPayment:withAuthenticationContext:returnURL:completion:` from the historical iOS example (old raw lines 99-137 and source lines 58–68) and forwards it to the newer `handleNextActionForPaymentIntent:authenticationContext:returnURL:completion:` path (`STPPaymentHandler.swift:398-411`). The `stripe-android` snapshot `2026-10-27-bb0d8d0` identifies 23.25.1 (`gradle.properties:24-27`). It retains `handleNextActionForPayment` and `onPaymentResult`, with an AndroidX `ComponentActivity` activity overload and a separate fragment overload (`Stripe.kt:280-329,344-368`). The enclosing plain `Activity` sample is historical (old raw lines 285-309 and source lines 70–75). Keep the iOS deprecation and Android host signature distinct from the React Native removal.

The April raw create-and-confirm examples send `payment_method_types: ["card"]` (old raw lines 32-40, 155-164, 218-226 and 414-422), even though the mapped source's shorter example at lines 23–31 omits that field. The separate Endive changelog (`raw/stripe-changelog-endive-2026-09-30-removes-the-payment-method-types-parameter-from-payment-intents-and-setup-intents-2026-11-07.md:5-24,28,34-36`) documents the named `2026-09-30.endive` PaymentIntent create endpoint rejecting writable `payment_method_types` with HTTP 400 and `payment_method_types_no_longer_supported`. Cite the named endpoint links and REST change table for Endive because Impact names `2026-08-26.preview`. Put the warning alongside the historical raw route (source lines 89–91) without changing the April guide's separately documented `confirmation_method` and `use_stripe_sdk` roles.

findings: The summary wiki/sources/source-stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments.md:17 should distinguish written permission and terms from a Stripe Mandate payload and from explicit customer authorization of the local merchant-of-record provider. The May Checkout branch calls for an upfront opt-in and a retained written agreement. Off-session terms include scope, anticipated frequency/timing and amount determination, plus cancellation policy for subscriptions. Checkout requires authorizing the local provider for future payments (raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:29-46,60-94). The Nigeria overview (raw/stripe-payments-countries-nigeria-2026-11-07.md:5-15,76-83,105-117) separately supplies partner identity, invite-request scope and the Naira card matrix, without proving account eligibility or a payment. Partner-MoR differs from Stripe Managed Payments (wiki/sources/source-stripe-nigeria-payment-methods.md:14-23; wiki/concepts/stripe-nigeria-payment-methods.md:8-14,40-42).

May Checkout creates a setup-mode Session for the Stripe Customer, which the merchant maps to its user. Test success is the SetupIntent transition from requires_action to succeeded (raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:42-94). Direct API setup creates an ng_card SetupIntent with Customer and usage, passes the SetupIntent secret to browser Stripe.js, and shows confirmNgCardSetup with return_url and online infer_from_client (raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:110-151,220-270). Separate charge-and-save starts/attempts a PaymentIntent with Customer, confirm and setup_future_usage=off_session, a return URL and optional mandate_data. Its sample includes explicit IP/user agent, NGN and automatic capture (raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:332-370). These are distinct setup, payment and consent identities. The current summary wiki/sources/source-stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments.md:24,28-35 should scope the successful SetupIntent transition to the successful test/setup outcome and keep redirects distinct from that outcome.

The baseline wiki/sources/source-stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments.md:35 and wiki/concepts/stripe-nigeria-payment-methods.md:58-59 overstate a code sample as a mandate_data requirement. The May PaymentIntent prose explicitly says optional mandate_data (raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:339-367), and the distinct November Create PaymentIntent reference says the object is optional and usable with confirm=true (raw/stripe-api-payment-intents-create-2026-11-07.md:627-650). The May browser SetupIntent sample infers acceptance metadata from the client (raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:248-265). A separately captured November Billing SetupIntents variant performs server confirmation with explicit IP and user agent in its example and then uses Stripe.js for the redirect/mandate authorization (raw/stripe-billing-subscriptions-ng-card-variant-c8486b9656-2026-11-07.md:36-58). Date and qualify by route/client-server role, retaining consumer's written permission regardless of optional request payload. The typed field, recorded permission and authorized mandate are separate.

In the manual redirect branch, require both PaymentIntent.status=requires_action and next_action.type=redirect_to_url, then take the redirect URL from that next_action. Browser return can include the PaymentIntent ID and client secret. Use server webhook status to verify payment outcome (raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:272-330). The mapped source and reciprocal concept omit the status check and verification boundary (wiki/sources/source-stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments.md:37-39; wiki/concepts/stripe-nigeria-payment-methods.md:63-65). The later charge makes and confirms a new PaymentIntent using the saved PaymentMethod ID from the preceding Intent and its Customer, with off_session=true when the customer is absent. Server detach deactivates the reusable payment method and sends mandate.updated and payment_method.detached (raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:372-396). The current summary wiki/sources/source-stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments.md:41-47 should distinguish conditional off_session and detach from payment outcomes or subscription cancellation.

The mapped source reproduces historical writable payment_method_types across Checkout setup, SetupIntent creation, charge-and-save and saved reuse (wiki/sources/source-stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments.md:23-43). Preserve the May examples in context, including standalone manual redirect, with a reciprocal API-version warning. The May requests send the field on Checkout Session Create (raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:79-90), SetupIntent Create (raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:133-147), and PaymentIntent Create (raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:272-295,339-368,372-392). The separate November-captured Checkout changelog documents HTTP 400 on Checkout Session Create at its linked 2026-09-30.endive endpoint and retains payment_method_types in the response (raw/stripe-changelog-endive-2026-09-30-remove-payment-method-types-checkout-sessions-2026-11-07.md:5-23). The Intent changelog's 2026-09-30.endive Create links and REST table document HTTP 400 with payment_method_types_no_longer_supported for the state-changing request, while the PaymentIntent/SetupIntent property remains read-only. Preserve that changelog's separate Impact reference to 2026-08-26.preview as a version ambiguity (raw/stripe-changelog-endive-2026-09-30-removes-the-payment-method-types-parameter-from-payment-intents-and-setup-intents-2026-11-07.md:5-36). Recurring payments, Connect, full and partial refunds and standard settlement continue (old raw lines 8-73, 109-133; new raw lines 9-27, 47-95, 140-170, 210-222). SetupIntent creates the mandate, and the documented retrieval follows SetupIntent.mandate to GET /v1/mandates/{id}. Checkout and Payment Element collect terms acceptance, while any non-Stripe-hosted collection must present the terms and confirm acceptance. A customer may cancel via bank or business. Detach the PaymentMethod to inactivate the associated Stripe mandate and collect a new DDA before new authorized debits. mandate.updated can also mark it inactive after permanent failure (old raw lines 75-85, 121-133; new raw lines 140-170 and 265-281).

The November product/UI/API grid specifies hosted full page and Checkout Sessions as recommended, also lists Payment Links, embedded form, Payment Element, Billing, Invoicing, Customer Portal, Connect, Payment Intents including setup_future_usage and Setup Intents, and explicitly excludes Express Checkout Element, Payment Method Messaging Element, in-app payments, Managed Payments, Radar, Terminal and off-session payments. Capture also expands specific authorization/capture exclusions and specifies no partial disputes (old raw lines 32-69; new raw lines 71-95 and 172-196). These table labels neither date launches nor resolve the linked off-session examples.

Refund handling now distinguishes a pre-submission request that cancels the payment from a post-submission request that remains pending until payment success. The latter is described as failed if the debit fails. Retrieve the Refund to track it. May said a refund requested before completion starts at PaymentIntent succeeded and is marked canceled if PaymentIntent enters requires_payment_method (old raw lines 183-193; new raw lines 96-122). Preserve both dated states and avoid treating the old canceled and new failed descriptions as interchangeable API outcomes.

New explicit DDA collection, retrieval and detachment steps, no-later-than-debit notice wording and immediate default confirmation description refine prior mandate policy and implementation (old raw lines 121-167; new raw lines 140-170, 224-255). Billing documents one automatic insufficient-funds retry within 30 days of the original attempt for configured recurring or one-off invoices and no debit failure fee on automatically initiated retries. May called it private preview, November drops the label but does not establish GA (old raw lines 195-197; new raw lines 257-263).

November adds statement descriptor precedence and 12-character truncation, then account business name and Stripe as fallback. Direct charges use the connected account. Destination and separate charges and transfers use the platform even with on_behalf_of, and actual statement may say Stripe New Zealand Limited (new raw lines 283-301).

Correct source line 17 and concept line 14 and link the dated Smart Retries companion. The request value `best_available` asks Stripe to apply an eligible retry strategy. The Smart Retries guide documents response `smart` for Smart Retries, `scheduled` for a custom schedule, and `heuristic` for Direct Debit, where AI retries are unavailable (Smart Retries companion lines 27-61). An OffSessionPayment can have `pending_retry`, but hard declines such as `authentication_required` cannot be retried automatically (lines 63-73 and 86-98). A retry option or failed attempt does not imply AI retry, an automatic reattempt for hard declines, or eventual success. Stripe attempts authorization asynchronously after returning the create response. A separate v2 event destination receives notifications for authorization attempts and other state changes (integration companion lines 14-16 and 133-135). The subscription, table and payload use the singular `v2.payments.off_session_payment.*` namespace despite the pluralized prose at line 139. `created` reflects the accepted create request, `attempt_started` marks an initial or retry authorization attempt, `attempt_failed` indicates a retryable failed attempt with retries remaining, and `failed` marks terminal failure. `succeeded` is sent after successful authorization for automatic capture or after calling the capture endpoint for manual capture (integration companion lines 24-35, 42-53 and 137-156). Those events do not establish settlement or payout.

Old transition lines 26-46, November transition lines 27-53, November Charges lines 27-53, and detailed card migration lines 15-37. In the November Charges card example, Stripe.js tokenizes card details in the browser. The merchant sends that Token to its server, which creates the Charge. findings: Both dated captures document a default HTTP 400 orchestration_unsupported response identifying the first unsupported feature. The summary’s line 19 needs a baseline correction: the onboarding opt-in, enabled through a Stripe representative, reroutes an unsupported request to Stripe instead of the originally determined processor. Error protection is considered during cross-processor retries and ignored only if there was failover and the original processor was Stripe, to avoid a duplicate Stripe attempt.

Both guides enable orchestration on server-side PaymentIntent creation through payments_orchestration.enabled=true. Billing, Checkout Sessions, Payment Links and Dashboard payments generate PaymentIntents and can use rules after representative configuration. Setup Intents API remains unsupported, flexible acquiring on other processors is unsupported, and a 3DS request requires the Acquirer BIN for the destination processor (old raw lines 32-55, new raw lines 50-67).

Both guides verify test routing through Processor and Recent activity in the Dashboard, or by retrieving the PaymentIntent's Payment Record ID and checking processor_details via the records API or Workbench. The sample Payment Record ID stays stable through a PaymentIntent lifecycle while the latest Payment Attempt Record represents an attempt generated on confirmation, and a third-party routed payment's latest_charge is null. Charges and Balance Transactions are absent for third-party volume. Underlying funds do not move through the Stripe account. Charge-dependent reporting or reconciliation uses Payment Attempt Records across all Stripe volume (old raw lines 57-117 and 128-155, new raw lines 69-155 and 178-206).

Externally handled card payments can be processing and trigger payment_intent.processing. They transition to succeeded with payment_intent.succeeded after the processor reports capture. An existing fulfillment handler based on succeeded needs no change according to both captures. Processing can support a temporary inventory hold. Checkout Return URL, routing, capture and Stripe-balance settlement are distinct facts. Dashboard analytics have up to two days' delay and lack balance summary/activity reports, dispute status or receipts for external volume (old raw lines 120-169, new raw lines 157-220).

November documents processor account selection within a rule action. The selected main or retry processor must support overrides. In Processor account logic choose Override processor account, then choose a configured account for that processor. Main and retry choices are independent and an unset choice falls back to the processor account logic from onboarding. An absent needed account is referred to Stripe, not created by this UI. Account means a configured account of the selected processor, not a new processor, Stripe customer, or Connect routing account. Duplicate and deactivate use the environment-specific overflow actions and require confirming the dialog. Old raw 34–58 and new raw 63–87. November retains the ten broadly prohibited categories and adds a code-level table treating prohibited MCCs as unsupported and restricted MCCs as potentially supported with additional information at account creation (old raw lines 150-175, new raw lines 18-37,39-160,174-190). May asks for a publicly accessible website or app, priced product/service list, company identifiers and refund/privacy policy links, with a warning about suspension or termination for category or site violations (old raw lines 167-175). November omits the May priced-list and public-access wording and does not expressly withdraw it.

May labels the family authenticated bank debit and describes standard payout timing (old raw lines 12-38). November labels it bank redirects, with immediate confirmation, instant provisional access and settlement up to T+2 business days (new raw lines 7-15). Preserve the dated label change and distinguish payment confirmation, provisional access, settlement and merchant payout. No replatforming or payout SLA is established. May's 180 days is a refund submission limit, not a merchant return promise or completion time (old raw lines 177-183, new raw lines 208-231).

findings: The source's main structure is dated correctly and mostly retains documented behavior (wiki/sources/source-stripe-partial-authorization.md:13-47), but its general debit/prepaid shorthand at line 13 and the catalog descriptor (wiki/stripe-index.md:573,708) need to preserve issuer/card dependence and the distinct May 2024 Amex and Visa examples. Latest expanded Charge card details provide partial_authorization.status (partially_authorized, fully_authorized, declined, not_requested), amount_requested and amount_authorized. The opt-in is a request. Its issuer-decline example returns card_declined. The $100-to-$70 manual example shows PaymentIntent requires_capture, zero amount_received and an uncaptured Charge until capture. Under manual capture the Intent amount/amount_capturable bounds the capture, and the successful example then has 7000 received and status succeeded. Under auto-capture the example ends succeeded with only 7000 captured and received. The mapped source wiki/sources/source-stripe-partial-authorization.md:29-43 should expose this operational boundary. Charge authorization, a captured partial amount, full order payment and funds availability are distinct. See raw/stripe-partial-authorization-2026.md:59-131,153-181 and raw/stripe-payments-partial-authorization-2026-11-07.md:52-124,138-168.

The mapped summary's incremental section (wiki/sources/source-stripe-partial-authorization.md:45-47) skips the separate request_incremental_authorization opt-in and confirmed uncaptured eligibility checkpoint. Read incremental_authorization.status=available on the latest Charge before the example increment, keep original partial opt-in inheritance and the explicit never override, and use amount as the desired new total. The example requests 150 USD total after initial 100 USD, approves 35 USD more (135 USD total), and leaves 135 USD capturable and 0 received. Preserve separate capture. See raw/stripe-partial-authorization-2026.md:183-285, raw/stripe-payments-partial-authorization-2026-11-07.md:170-270, and the separate increment guide raw/stripe-incremental-authorization-2026.md:729-745. Apply the two options at their distinct stages so the partial opt-in is not mistaken for enabling incremental authorization itself.

Both captures prohibit overcapture above the partially approved amount, cap the transfer_amount when it exceeds the partial approval on a charge on behalf of a Connect account, and decline below Stripe's minimum. See raw/stripe-partial-authorization-2026.md:26-32 and raw/stripe-payments-partial-authorization-2026-11-07.md:27-33. The source wiki/sources/source-stripe-partial-authorization.md:25-27 retains the boundaries. Preserve the reciprocal overcapture warning at wiki/concepts/stripe-overcapture.md:14-18,41-60 and wiki/sources/source-stripe-overcapture.md:15-19,62-66, where a general overcapture route or allowed percentage does not override this feature's restriction.

November replaces the Node samples with form-encoded curl REST samples for initial manual/auto confirmation, capture and initial incremental-enabled confirmation. Initial creation samples omit the prior explicit payment_method_types=['card'] and include return_url with confirm=true. Those are visible request-example changes, with no statement changing the online-card scope, required payment method fields or feature availability. The standalone versioned Create API describes return_url as optional, used with confirm=true for a return after authentication or cancellation (raw/stripe-api-payment-intents-create-2026-11-07.md:669-670). A return is not authorization, capture, or fulfillment evidence. The general default does not establish partial-authorization compatibility with automatic_async, and the sample does not establish equivalence or a universal default. Retain both version references and warn readers against copying the May field to the documented Endive Create endpoint. The November partial-authorization curl examples omit that field but specify neither API version nor cause.

findings: November is a two-link selector preserving the page purpose and old route identifiers (new lines 5-14; old lines 4-18; diff lines 7-19 and 49-50). It routes Checkout Sessions using `payment-ui=embedded-components` and Payment Intents using `payment-ui=elements`; these documentation selectors do not establish a `ui_mode` API value or any current route behavior.

Old April overview recommends Checkout Sessions for most integrations and limits the deferred/eager and client/server choices to the Payment Intents variant (old lines 8-26). Source lines 13-15 correctly identify the detailed scope but risk presenting the full guide as exclusively Payment Intents; retain both dated routes and label the two choices variant-specific.

April deferred creates the Payment Element first and Intent after submission, suitable for multi-page or changing amounts affecting method eligibility. Eager creates the PaymentIntent or SetupIntent before page load and passes its `client_secret` into Elements. Current source line 22's 'together' compresses this order and client association (old lines 28-38). The Intent identities differ: PaymentIntent collects payment; SetupIntent sets up a method for next use.

April server confirmation does not eliminate pending customer actions: the merchant must handle required next actions manually or via an SDK, for example `stripe.handleNextAction` in the cited PaymentIntent route (old lines 40-48). Source lines 30-33 and concept lines 43-48 omit this consequence. Client confirmation uses the SDK for supported next actions and localization. 'No server-side business logic required' should mean no need for server control at confirmation, not no backend.

Root index line 7 leads via Stripe index lines 73-74 and 729 to Payment Intents concept lines 30-55 and 139. Companion May server-confirmation source lines 15-23 and raw lines 689-703 verify that a server result may still require client handling. Reuse the existing route, date the detailed guidance, and link the related server guide.
historical_claims_to_preserve: April Checkout Sessions recommendation and Checkout's own client initialization, SDK/provider and confirmation, qualified to its dated route and captured `ui_mode: elements` example. Keep Checkout Session secret and Intent secret distinct. April early recommendation and its Adaptive Pricing wording are not re-attested by a selector (old lines 8-20).

April multi-page/dynamic deferred path, static eager path, and action handling identities remain dated (old 28-48). Preserve immediate server confirmation after pre-confirmation business decisions (payment method restrictions or application fees), together with required next actions if returned.

Payment data associated at confirmation does not establish successful payment or setup. The no-charge SetupIntent purpose is different from PaymentIntent payment collection; required action may follow confirmation (old 30, 40-48).
conflicts: Mapped source line 30 broadly says no server-side business logic, while old lines 44-45 only say additional control at confirmation is unnecessary for that path. Current source lines 31-33 and concept lines 47-48 omit pending next-action responsibilities described at old line 47. A server-response/confirmation route cannot be treated as eliminating authentication or proving payment.

Current source line 22 and concept line 39 say create both together without the before-load/Intent secret association condition (old lines 37-38). Checkout Sessions initializing its own SDK (old line 8) and PaymentIntent/SetupIntent initializing Elements (old 37) are separate paths; do not substitute one secret or confirmation function for the other.

conflicts: Source line 86's 'client_secret (server-only, TLS required)' contradicts both the historical and November delivery instructions (old raw lines 25-27, 50-125 and new raw lines 28-30, 49-101). Server create/retrieve and deliver the intent-scoped client secret to that customer through a TLS-protected SPA endpoint or SSR form. Keep secret API keys and the complete object off the browser, avoid logging or merchant embedding the secret in URLs, and distinguish the April Stripe.js quickstart's provider-appended return-page query (raw/stripe-payment-intents-quickstart-2025.md lines 190-205, Payment Intents concept line 55). The latter is for display/status retrieval and supplies no fulfillment or logging permission.

Source lines 17, 22-24, 31-40 and 55-61 oversimplify the lifecycle. PaymentIntent creation tracks an attempt to collect; server creation or confirmation alone does not prove successful charge. requires_action can be additional action such as 3DS, not limited to 3DS. Processing can be delayed; authorization can instead leave requires_capture before capture; SetupIntent saves without charge and its successful status establishes setup, not payment. Attribute the original 'immediate' wording to purpose versus the actual async path from the separately dated lifecycle authority (April raw/stripe-payment-setup-intents-2025.md lines 10-18, 24-54 and 58-86; November corresponding lifecycle lines 13-35), and state the branches accurately.

Source lines 25 and 71-73 summarize general cancellation and the limited processing exception. Scope it to the PaymentIntent rather than assuming direct cancellation for every Checkout Session. The separate November Cancel reference lines 7-11 documents direct cancellation of a Checkout Session's PaymentIntent only in requires_capture, otherwise expire the Session. Its example specifies 2026-10-28.endive at lines 20-25. Retain both scope statements and apply no blanket cancellation guarantee.

Both guide captures pair shorthand about no double charges/idempotency with explicit cart-bound idempotency keys (old raw lines 12-17 and 42-48; new raw lines 15-20, 41-47). The separate November Payment Intents API reference lines 80-85 scopes at most one successful Charge to one PaymentIntent. Multiple attempts can produce multiple Charge objects (old raw lines 127-131; new raw lines 103-107). Qualify Payment Intents concept line 10 so it does not imply duplicate creation cannot occur, and add a direct locator for creation/reuse/key best practices in the mapped source.

The dated checkout comparison at source lines 63-69 should distinguish a Checkout Session client secret initializing ui_mode=elements from a PaymentIntent secret used with Stripe.js/Elements and its confirmation. Keep the captured React @stripe/react-stripe-js/checkout CheckoutElementsProvider and checkout.confirm path, and the HTML initCheckoutElementsSdk plus loadActions path, scoped as documented examples. The reciprocal Checkout Sessions source lines 33-48 preserves ui_mode=custom as literally printed by its separate overview samples and distinguishes the versioned React elements path. Read alongside Checkout concept lines 34-81 for exact package boundaries. The compared Payment Intents guide gives no general SDK version guarantee and does not establish deprecation of Payment Intents.

The lead-in suggests statement_descriptor for card charges in both captures, while their code and explicit note use statement_descriptor_suffix for card and statement_descriptor for non-card (old raw lines 161-182; new raw lines 133-149). The November Create reference lines 690-700 confirms that statement_descriptor on cards errors. Add the reciprocal API-reference warning and keep the 22-character combined prefix, separator and suffix rule. November cURL omission of April's explicit card array in this and the metadata sample does not change supported payment methods.

April 19 descriptor and metadata examples send writable payment_method_types on PaymentIntent Create (old raw lines 165-176 and 196-209). November's cURL examples omit it and provide no API version or reason (new raw lines 137-143 and 163-169). The November-captured Endive changelog (raw/stripe-changelog-endive-2026-09-30-removes-the-payment-method-types-parameter-from-payment-intents-and-setup-intents-2026-11-07.md lines 5-36) documents HTTP 400 / payment_method_types_no_longer_supported on the linked 2026-09-30.endive PaymentIntent Create endpoint and retains the read-only object property. Its Impact heading also names 2026-08-26.preview, so do not claim the first affected API version. Preserve dated April examples and add a reciprocal warning alongside the separate exact-version stripe@23.0.0 SDK boundary at Payment Intents concept lines 125-127.

Correct the unconditional '3DS on SetupIntent creates a mandate' wording at source lines 22 and 61. The April and November lifecycle pages use compressed, dated authentication/mandate phrasing (raw/stripe-payment-setup-intents-2025.md lines 10-18 and raw/stripe-payments-paymentintents-lifecycle-2026-11-07.md lines 13-19). The separately bundled April 19 Setup Intents guide (raw/stripe-setup-intents-api-2025.md lines 28-50 and 52-68) distinguishes applicable authentication, explicit customer consent for future on-session use, and an upfront agreement or mandate for future off-session charging. 3DS alone supplies neither mandate consent nor a guaranteed later SCA exemption. SetupIntent usage describes intended reuse for setup without payment. PaymentIntent setup_future_usage is the separate field for saving during a payment (old raw lines 133-159 and new raw lines 109-131). The issuer can still require authentication or reject a later charge. Keep the dated simplified wording as source evidence and route this distinction in the combined summary.

conflicts: Old event link text and href conflict (old line 74); new line 84 aligns them. Preserve old provenance and warn readers opening the old raw to follow `charge.updated`, not `charge.created`.
